feedback.claim: The draft is inconsistent about whether League Administrators can assign, reassign, or revoke League Administrator assignments, leaving mutation authority for the top-level administrative role ambiguous.
feedback.evidence: Core Mutation Authority says League Administrators may "assign, reassign, and revoke role assignments," and Role Assignment Lifecycle says a League Administrator assignment persists until revoked. Audit Configuration also lists "League Administrator and Team Captain assignment changes" as audited. However Authorization Configuration narrows assignment authority to "League Administrators assign, reassign, and revoke Team Captain authority," and Invariants / Authorization says only a League Administrator may "assign Team Captain authority" without naming League Administrator assignment mutation. The scope contract marks scoped authorization and minimum audit behavior as in scope at required_fields depth.
feedback.recommended_change: Make League Administrator assignment mutation authority explicit and consistent across lifecycle, invariants, and config. Either state that Phase 1 includes League Administrator assignment creation/revocation by an existing League Administrator with audited rules, including any bootstrap boundary if needed, or state that League Administrator assignment mutation beyond persistence/revocation is deferred and cannot be inferred from the generic role-assignment language.
feedback.severity_rationale: This does not obscure the whole MVP domain, but it creates meaningful implementation risk for the administrative authority boundary that controls every core mutation surface.

feedback.claim: Concurrent first-freeze behavior depends on whether attempts use the same result-affecting configuration basis, but the draft does not define a canonical identity or equality rule for that basis.
feedback.evidence: The Season Configuration Lifecycle says a competing first-freeze attempt must reuse the created snapshot when it depends on the same result-affecting configuration basis, or be rejected when it depends on a different mutable configuration basis. Authority and Precedence repeats this rule, but neither section defines how the configuration basis is canonically compared, hashed, or otherwise identified for replay and concurrent duplicate detection. The scope contract explicitly allows pressure on deterministic calculations and configuration versioning.
feedback.recommended_change: Define the result-affecting configuration basis as an exact canonical value set or content identity for the in-scope result-affecting fields, and require concurrent/retried freeze attempts to compare that canonical basis identity. State that equal canonical basis identities reuse the existing frozen version and unequal basis identities are rejected without mutating authoritative state.
feedback.severity_rationale: The first freeze is part of the core finalize/forfeit flow and determines which configuration version all later standings and playoff calculations replay. Without a deterministic basis identity, implementers can diverge under retries or concurrency.
